name: Segmental Spinal Dysgenesis

criteria.description: Congenital focal agenesis or dysgenesis of one or more segments of the lumbar or thoracolumbar spine
Segmental abnormality of the spinal cord corresponding to vertebral anomalies, including hypoplasia or absence
Neurological deficits affecting lower limbs such as spasticity, weakness, or paralysis
Presence of associated congenital anomalies such as vertebral segmentation defects or tethered cord

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital segmental vertebral malformation with corresponding spinal cord abnormality and clinical neurological deficits in lower limbs
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging findings correlated with clinical neurological presentation.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Segmental agenesis or hypoplasia of the spinal cord
searchTerms: missing or underdeveloped spinal cord segments
spinal cord segments not fully formed

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital focal vertebral malformations in lumbar or thoracolumbar regions
searchTerms: birth defects in lower spine bones
malformed lumbar or lower thoracic vertebrae
increased muscle tone in lower limbs

common.symptomName: Lower limb muscle weakness or paralysis
Gait abnormalities including difficulty walking or inability to walk

searchTerms: loss of feeling in lower limbs
permanent bending of lower limb joints

rare.symptomName: Respiratory complications due to thoracic involvement
searchTerms: lung complications due to chest involvement

imaging: MRI showing segmental absence or hypoplasia of spinal cord
X-ray or CT demonstrating focal vertebral agenesis or malformations
Ultrasound or urodynamic studies indicating neurogenic bladder
genetic: No consistent genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases predominate
other: Clinical neurological examination revealing lower limb motor and sensory deficits

distinguishingFeatures: More extensive sacral and lower lumbar agenesis
Absence of segmental spinal cord abnormalities
Open neural tube defect with meningeal sac

redFlags: Progressive lower limb weakness or paralysis
Loss of bladder or bowel control
references: Kothbauer KF, et al. Segmental spinal dysgenesis: clinical and radiological features. Neurosurgery. 1998.
Sankar WN, et al. Segmental spinal dysgenesis: a review of the literature. J Pediatr Orthop. 2010.
